title: Placed Consumer Accounts Closure Standard: Paid in Full, Settled in Full, Letters and Refunds
content:
Account Closure desk standard for **Placed Consumer Accounts**: when an account closes as paid in full or settled in full, when the closure letter may be issued, statements of account, and how an overpayment is refunded.

## Standard

**1. Paid in full.** An account closes as paid in full on the day payments, direct payments and client credits bring the balance due to exactly zero.

**2. Settled in full.** An account closes as settled in full on the day an accepted settlement is fulfilled, when the remaining balance due is waived in one settlement waiver entry whose amount equals that remaining balance due. A waiver is booked only for a settlement whose status is fulfilled, once per settlement; the settlement's status is read from Ridgeline's settlement record.

**3. Closure letters.** A paid-in-full letter or settled-in-full letter is issued once per account and only after the final payment has cleared. A closure letter is issued only when the handling date is later than the clearance period counted from the final payment's date. The clearance period is the stage's clearance figure for the final payment's channel, counted in business days after the payment date, business days being Monday through Friday excluding US federal legal public holidays:

| Final payment channel | Clearance figure used |
|---|---|
| ACH bank debit | ACH clearance |
| Debit card or credit card | Card clearance |
| Mailed check | Mailed-check clearance |
| Money order | Money-order clearance |
| Retail cash payment network | Cash payment network clearance |

The letter is then issued within the stage's closure letter time, in business days, by email when the consumer asks and the profile carries an email address, otherwise by mail.

**4. Account status for letters and statements.** Closure letters and statements are issued only for accounts whose status is validation period, active, arranged, dispute hold, hardship hold, paid in full or settled in full. A statement of account may be issued on any date at the consumer's request, free of charge.

**5. Overpayment refunds.** An overpayment is refunded within the stage's overpayment refund time, in business days after the payment that created it: to the same card for card payments, to the same bank account for ACH payments, and by mailed check for mailed-check, money-order and cash-network payments.

## Refund route at a glance

| Payment that created the overpayment | Refund goes |
|---|---|
| Debit card or credit card | To the same card |
| ACH bank debit | To the same bank account |
| Mailed check, money order or retail cash payment network | By mailed check |

## Hypothetical clearance case

*Primary Placement's 5-business-day card clearance from the Placed Consumer Accounts closure schedule; the dates are invented and fall in a month with no US federal legal public holiday.*

A final debit-card payment dated Monday 2026-03-02 brings the account to zero. The five business days after it are March 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9, so the clearance period ends on 2026-03-09.
- Handling date 2026-03-09: the paid-in-full letter is not yet issued.
- Handling date 2026-03-10: the letter may be issued.

## Basis questions

**Does a consumer pay for a statement of account?** No; it is free of charge and may be issued on any date at the consumer's request, for an account in one of the statuses in paragraph 4.

**May a second paid-in-full letter be issued on the same account?** No; the letter is issued once per account.
